milestone: Catalog coverage verified 26/26 — every published package has an entry either merged or in an open PR
the_gap_found: onboarding-check was published at 0.1.0 and had no entry anywhere. With twenty-six packages across three repositories, 'did every package get an entry' is precisely the kind of thing that drifts silently: nothing anywhere reports it, and the package is simply invisible in Discover forever. Closed by PR #16509.

tool.what: derives each package's expected entry filename from the catalog's own slugFor rule, then checks upstream main and named PR branches for it
bugs_found_while_writing_it: execFile's default 1 MB maxBuffer cannot hold the 11k-path upstream tree; the failure surfaced as 'Command failed', which points at the API rather than at the buffer
the bulk tree response does not survive this network resetting mid-transfer, so the design moved to per-file contents lookups (a few hundred bytes each)
PR branches live on the fork, not upstream — checking ref against the upstream repo answered 'does main have it' and reported every open entry as missing
tool.known_limit: the all-branches mode is slow here (sequential calls on a resetting link); for a one-off audit the parallel shell loop over package→branch pairs is faster. The script earns its keep as a periodic check, not as a per-round tool.

verification: 17 entries found in branches (13 unique pending plus 4 whose PR merged but whose branch still exists), 13 on main, no package without an entry
